caveats: Held-out attacks were never shown to the auto-policy generator; their results measure generalisation, not training fit.
The reply stage only withholds final answers containing known canary values or system-prompt marker phrases. A paraphrase would pass.
A control counts as a false positive only when a detector fires. Benign calls blocked by policy are reported separately as controls.after.blocked_calls.
Everything is simulated: no real file, email, shell or network access.

v2 adds an argument-level data-loss stage on top of v1: it scans URLs (decoded query string included), email subject/body and shell commands for canaries and deny-listed file content, after URL, base64 and hex decoding.

v2 only recognises protected content at least 16 characters long (policies/v2.yaml: min_fragment_length). A secret split into shorter pieces can still leave, and the raw canary detector cannot see the pieces either.
The baseline detector does not decode encodings, so a base64 or split leak is invisible at baseline even when v2 blocks it. Read v2.attacks for the per-channel detail rather than the ASR alone.
